newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Huili hurt by poison rumours.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Huili hurt by poison rumours.

text.p: China's paint producer Shanghai Huili Building Materials Co Ltd is suffering plummeting sales of its main paint and coating products because of rumours that they contain poison, an official said on Wednesday.

The rumours stem from an incident in the southwest province of Sichuan last year in which a man died in his sleep in his freshly painted room. The word spread that the wall coating was made by Huili and sales began to fall.

"We sent people out to check on the case and it appears the man had been drinking and may have become too excited with his girlfriend," said company accountant Wang Ruili in an interview. "It had nothing to do with the coating on the walls."
"We have done tests and there is no poison in the coatings at all, it is just rumours," she added.
But the poison rumours were already out and Huili, which listed B shares on the Shanghai stock exchange in June, saw sales of its coatings start to fall from the second half of last year.
Coatings accounted for 50 percent of the company's profits before the rumours but have now dropped to 40 percent and are still falling.
Overall profits are falling too as a result. The company reported a net profit of 80 million yuan ($9.64 million) in 1994, but only 48 million in 1995.
"The first half of this year was bad. The second half will be better, but we will still see a further fall in profits. The main reason is the rumours," Wang said.
A secondary factor affecting sales, she said, was widespread piracy of Huili products, particularly by factories in the southern Guangdong province. ($1=8.3 yuan)
